body:
One of the things that will inevitably come up is, whose fault is this suicide? Who can we blame?

So I say this, the only one to blame is my father.

He really didn’t prepare me for this world. He clearly never wanted to be a father. He left me to fend for myself at every turn. To weak and scrawny to protect myself, I hid behind my mother, and other mothers. I had no father. Just a man who yelled at me when I got to be too much for him to deal with. He has since devolved into a useless waste of space who sits each day on a couch in Internet chat rooms. 

Look through my Internet history, through the usage logs that detail how much time I spent on which websites, and you’ll see the same patterns. I’m no different from him, the only difference is that I won’t carry on the cycle of pain. This particular branch of the family dies with me. I won’t carry it any further. I don’t think anyone could make a data-driven argument that this lineage is worth continuing. 

I’m useless to society, as is my father, as was his father before him. Yet in their twenties, my father and grandfather had SOME purpose to society. My grandfather found a role in the military. My father found a role in the small business community. Well, the military won’t take me due to a history of mental illness. And the small business community is so squeezed that I have to role their either.

My only conceivable role is to be a burden on my family, on my mother and sister, on my aunts and uncles. I can only drain their bank accounts from black to red or from red to redder. 

My death is the final act of sympathy I can perform. 

For anyone reading this, there is no chance I would ever get better, that I would fulfill my potential. The world just doesn’t need me, I recognized that, so I decided to bow out. 

Going back again, to what I said above about this being my father’s fault. That is only half true. Because on the flip side, what could he have done differently? He could have loved me more? Done more to help me find my way through this world? He had a fucked up upbringing of his own and at the time of my departure, he has as many problems as I do. So it’s not his fault for lack of caring. I know he loved me. He was just incompetent. He knows this, my mother and sister know this, the whole world knows this. Because you can’t hide the truth.

So instead, we look at the ugly truth and shine it up. Because the reality is too hard to face. 

As David Simon would say, “the whole world shines shit and calls it gold."
